text: June E Huh (Korean: 허준이; born June 9, 1983) is an American mathematician currently serving as a professor at Princeton University, having previously held a professorship at Stanford University. He received the Fields Medal and a MacArthur Fellowship in 2022, recognized for establishing connections between algebraic geometry and combinatorics. Huh was born in Stanford, California, while his parents were pursuing graduate studies at Stanford University; his family returned to South Korea when he was about two years old. His father was a professor of statistics at Korea University, and his mother was a professor of Russian language at Seoul National University. Poor performance on elementary school tests led him to believe he lacked mathematical aptitude, and he later dropped out of high school to focus on writing poetry after growing weary of routine studying. Described as a late bloomer, Huh enrolled at Seoul National University in 2002 but initially struggled with depression and poor academic performance. He initially aimed to become a science journalist, majoring in physics and astronomy, but had a poor attendance record and repeated courses. Early in his studies, he was mentored by Japanese mathematician Heisuke Hironaka, who was a visiting professor at Seoul National University. After failing several courses, Huh took an algebraic geometry course under Hironaka in his sixth year, focusing on singularity theory based on Hironaka’s current research, which sparked his interest in research-level mathematics. He completed a master's degree at Seoul National University while frequently traveling to Japan with Hironaka and serving as his personal assistant. Due to his undergraduate record, he was rejected by all but one American university and began his Ph.D. at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2009, transferring to the University of Michigan in 2011. He graduated in 2014 at age 31 with a thesis under Mircea Mustață and was awarded the Sumner Byron Myers Prize for his doctoral work. In 2009, during his Ph.D., Huh proved the Read–Hoggar conjecture, a 40-year-old unresolved problem in graph theory concerning the unimodality of coefficients of chromatic polynomials. In joint work with Karim Adiprasito and Eric Katz, he resolved the Heron–Rota–Welsh conjecture on the log-concavity of the characteristic polynomial of matroids. With Adiprasito, he is one of five recipients of the 2019 New Horizons in Mathematics Prize, linked to the Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics. He won the Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists (U.S. Regional) in 2017 and was an invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Rio de Janeiro in 2018. In 2021, he received the Samsung Ho-Am Prize in Science for physics and mathematics. Huh was awarded the 2022 Fields Medal for bringing Hodge theory to combinatorics, proving the Dowling–Wilson conjecture for geometric lattices, resolving the Heron–Rota–Welsh conjecture for matroids, developing the theory of Lorentzian polynomials, and proving the strong Mason conjecture. He is the seventh recipient of East Asian ancestry and the first of Korean ancestry to receive the Fields Medal. Huh is married to Kim Nayoung, whom he met during his studies at Seoul National University; she earned her doctorate in mathematics from Seoul National University, and the couple has two sons.
